column17: name from Etruscan 'mouth' (at the mouth of the Arno); 5C Etruscan prince tomb proves Etruscan origin, Servius claims founding by the Teuti -1300 (legend); friendly Etruscan port used by Roman generals as departure point for Corsica, Ligurians had come back to the Arno in 3C and Roman ops against them N of the Arno begin -238 (NCAH VII_2.9 pp 432-3) (CAH VII.25 p 805); Roman colony as Portus Pisanus -180; municipium -89; under Augustus fortified and renamed Colonia Iulia obsequens; Baths of Nero 90s; after Charlemagne beats the Lombards 774 falls to duchy of Lucca; ships raid N Africa 828; taken by Vikings (Bjorn Ironside) 860; helps defend Salerno from Saracens 871; county centre in mark of Tuscia 930; helps Otto I and beats Byzantine fleet 970; first communal war in Italy (v Lucca) 1003; sacks Reggio Calabria 1005; with Genoa backs Sardinian giudicati v Saracen Mugahid 1017 and gains supremacy in the Tyrrhenian; conquers Carthage 1030-35; admiral Ciurini takes Corsica 1051-52; first battle with Genoa 1060 (Pisan win); takes Palermo from Saracens 1063; Gregory VII recognises Pisan sea laws 1077; Henry IV recognises commune 1081; takes Mahdia 1087; Urban II gives it archbishopric and supremacy over Corsica and Sardinia 1092; instrumental in taking Jerusalem 1099; war with Paschal II to free the Balearics from the Moors 1113; decline begins with defeat by Genoa at Meloria 6 Aug 1284; Genoa destroys Porto Pisano 1290; Sardinia lost to Aragon 1324; occupied by Florence 1405; independent as Second Pisan Republic 1494, ~15 yrs of sieges, then sold to the Visconti and eventually to Florence again; Kingdom of Etruria 1801; part of France 1807; Scuola Normale founded 1810; Habsburg-Lorraine restored 1815; heavily destroyed in WWII; guess start & stop; coords from memory, replace with Pleiades (Wiki 43 43N 10 24E) (Wiki "Pisa" 11/23/26)
